executiveSummary: Surveillance data spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas represents the highest-priority select agent concern, with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk flagged across two separate PAHO updates (November 2025 and March 2026). Mpox continues circulating in the Americas region as of April 2026, while dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and measles present simultaneous elevated burdens across Latin America. Respiratory virus co-circulation including influenza and RSV, combined with the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in April 2026, compounds healthcare system pressure across multiple regions.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover risk and concurrent multi-pathogen outbreaks across the Americas and Europe demand immediate coordinated surveillance and response escalation.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoir with pandemic potential
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in human infections
Ongoing circulation in poultry and wild birds across multiple American countries
threats.action: Immediate activation of One Health surveillance protocols; enhance human case detection at animal-human interfaces; ensure stockpiling of H5N1-specific antivirals and candidate vaccines; coordinate with FAO and OIE for animal reservoir control

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Active epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating ongoing transmission
Sustained community spread in the Americas requiring continued monitoring
Potential for clade-specific severity differences requiring clade surveillance
Select agent (BSL-3) with human-to-human transmission documented
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing; expand vaccination coverage with MVA-BN in high-risk populations; ensure clade typing for all confirmed cases; coordinate cross-border surveillance with ECDC given concurrent European monitoring

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating active risk
Potential sylvatic cycle expansion into peri-urban areas
Vaccine-preventable disease with high mortality if unvaccinated populations exposed
BSL-3 pathogen with hemorrhagic fever potential
threats.action: Urgent verification of vaccination coverage in at-risk zones; deploy emergency vaccination campaigns in outbreak areas; enhance entomological surveillance for Aedes and Haemagogus vectors; activate yellow fever vaccine stockpile through PAHO/WHO

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 18 2026 indicating elevated burden
Multi-serotype circulation increases risk of severe dengue through antibody-dependent enhancement
Ongoing vector expansion linked to climate-driven Aedes aegypti range shifts
Potential healthcare system strain from simultaneous respiratory virus co-circulation
threats.action: Intensify integrated vector management; strengthen severe dengue case management capacity; promote community-based larval source reduction; monitor serotype distribution for ADE risk assessment

threats.name: Measles
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026 indicating active transmission
Vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic creating susceptible cohorts
Highly contagious with R0 of 12-18 enabling rapid spread in under-vaccinated communities
Risk of reestablishing endemic transmission in previously eliminated regions
threats.action: Conduct emergency supplemental immunization activities targeting children under 5 and susceptible adolescents; investigate and close vaccination coverage gaps; strengthen case-based measles surveillance and laboratory confirmation

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating persistent elevated activity
Possible waning immunity from acellular pertussis vaccines driving resurgence
Infant deaths remain a key severity indicator in ongoing surveillance
Cyclical resurgence pattern consistent with regional trends
threats.action: Review and reinforce Tdap booster recommendations for adolescents and adults; prioritize vaccination of pregnant women for passive immunity transfer; enhance laboratory capacity for PCR confirmation; investigate potential role of vaccine-strain mismatch

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue complicates clinical diagnosis and case management
Aedes vector expansion increases geographic spread potential
Chronic arthralgia burden affects long-term population health and productivity
threats.action: Strengthen differential diagnosis capacity to distinguish from dengue; enhance vector control measures in affected areas; provide clinical guidance for managing chronic chikungunya arthralgia; monitor for novel lineage introduction

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: Southern Hemisphere influenza season start flagged by PAHO April 27 2026
RSV and influenza simultaneous circulation alert issued January 9 2026
Multiple ECDC weekly threat reports from April-May 2026 monitoring respiratory virus activity
Healthcare system strain from dual respiratory pathogen burden in vulnerable populations
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake before Southern Hemisphere peak season; ensure RSV prophylaxis availability for high-risk infants and elderly; strengthen ILI/SARI sentinel surveillance; maintain antiviral stockpiles and ICU capacity planning

selectAgentSummary: Three BSL-3/BSL-4 relevant pathogens were detected in this surveillance period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) (BSL-3 select agent) is the highest priority, with two PAHO updates confirming sustained animal reservoir activity and zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas through March 2026. Mpox virus (BSL-3) is actively circulating in the Americas as of April 2026 with ongoing human-to-human transmission. Yellow fever virus (BSL-3) triggered a PAHO epidemiological alert in March 2026 indicating active risk in the Americas. All three require enhanced biosafety protocols, specialized laboratory confirmation, and immediate public health response escalation.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR reports identified in current surveillance set; however Bordetella pertussis surveillance should include macrolide resistance monitoring given global trends
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) surveillance warranted given H5N1 activity and widespread antiviral use
Dengue co-infections with bacterial pathogens may mask antimicrobial stewardship opportunities in febrile illness management
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen alert burden in the Americas suggests systemic surveillance and healthcare capacity strain across the region
Two separate H5N1 PAHO updates within four months indicates persistent and potentially expanding zoonotic interface risk
Back-to-back pertussis updates suggest a resurgence wave potentially driven by vaccine immunity waning post-pandemic disruptions
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset coincides with peak dengue and chikungunya transmission creating compounded febrile illness diagnostic challenge
Misuse of GLP-1 receptor agonist medications alert (February 2026) signals emerging non-communicable drug safety threat requiring pharmacovigilance integration into health security frameworks
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) followed by ongoing communicable disease alerts suggests dual chemical and biological threat environment in the Americas
